Topic: AKS cluster autoscaler and node pools
Keywords: aks, cluster autoscaler, node pool, system pool
Guidance: Running application workloads on the AKS system node pool starves core cluster services (CoreDNS, metrics-server) of resources during load spikes.
Do: Separate system and user node pools, and enable the cluster autoscaler on user pools sized per workload.
Don't: Schedule application pods onto the default system node pool.
Example: az aks nodepool add --cluster-name myAKS --resource-group rg --name userpool --mode User --enable-cluster-autoscaler --min-count 2 --max-count 10

Topic: Azure Functions cold start and plan choice
Keywords: azure functions, consumption plan, premium plan, cold start
Guidance: The Consumption plan scales to zero, which means unpredictable cold-start latency; latency-sensitive functions need the Premium plan's pre-warmed instances instead.
Do: Use the Premium plan (or dedicated App Service plan) for latency-sensitive Functions; reserve Consumption for bursty/background workloads.
Don't: Put a synchronous, latency-sensitive API on the Consumption plan and expect consistent response times.
Example: az functionapp plan create --name premium-plan --resource-group rg --sku EP1

Keywords: arm template, bicep, iac, azure resource manager
Guidance: Hand-written raw ARM JSON is verbose and error-prone compared to Bicep, which compiles down to the same ARM templates with far better readability and type checking.
Do: Author new infrastructure in Bicep and transpile to ARM at deploy time rather than hand-writing ARM JSON.
Don't: Maintain new large ARM JSON templates by hand in 2026.

Keywords: azure devops, service connection, pipeline permissions, yaml pipeline
Guidance: Service connections scoped to subscription-level Owner/Contributor let any pipeline that uses them touch every resource in the subscription, not just its own resource group.
Do: Scope service connections to the specific resource group a pipeline needs, using least-privilege custom roles where possible.
Don't: Grant a shared service connection Owner rights at the subscription level for all pipelines.

Topic: Entra ID RBAC vs Owner role sprawl
Keywords: entra id, azure ad, rbac, owner role
Guidance: Assigning the built-in Owner role because it 'just works' is the Azure equivalent of AWS AdministratorAccess sprawl -- it grants role assignment rights too, letting a compromised identity self-escalate.
Do: Use built-in or custom roles scoped to required actions (e.g. Contributor without role-assignment rights) instead of Owner by default.
Don't: Assign Owner to service principals and users as a default starting point.

Keywords: blob storage, lifecycle policy, cool tier, archive tier
Guidance: Leaving all blobs in the Hot access tier forever, including logs and backups nobody reads after 30 days, is one of the most common sources of avoidable Azure storage cost.
Do: Configure lifecycle management policies to auto-tier blobs to Cool/Archive and expire old versions.
Don't: Leave lifecycle management unconfigured on storage accounts holding logs or backups.
Example: az storage account management-policy create --account-name mystorage --policy @policy.json

Topic: Key Vault access policies vs RBAC
Keywords: key vault, access policy, rbac, secrets
Guidance: Key Vault's legacy access-policy model grants all-or-nothing permissions per vault; the RBAC permission model allows fine-grained, auditable per-secret/per-key roles instead.
Do: Use Key Vault's Azure RBAC permission model with scoped role assignments instead of broad vault access policies.
Don't: Grant full get/list/set/delete access-policy permissions to every service that needs one secret.

Keywords: resource group, tags, cost allocation, governance
Guidance: Untagged resources scattered across ad-hoc resource groups make cost allocation and cleanup nearly impossible once an environment grows past a handful of services.
Do: Enforce mandatory tags (owner, environment, cost-center) via Azure Policy, and group resources by lifecycle, not by type.
Don't: Create resources without required tags and rely on memory to track ownership.

Topic: NSG rule ordering and VNet peering
Keywords: nsg, network security group, vnet peering, rule priority
Guidance: NSG rules are evaluated in priority order and stop at first match; a broad low-priority allow rule placed above a specific deny will silently override it.
Do: Order NSG rules from most-specific/restrictive to least, and use Azure Network Watcher to verify effective rules.
Don't: Add new NSG rules without checking their priority against existing broad rules.
Example: az network nsg rule create --nsg-name myNSG --name deny-ssh --priority 100 --access Deny --destination-port-ranges 22

Topic: Azure Cost Management budgets and alerts
Keywords: cost management, budget alert, azure advisor, cost anomaly
Guidance: Without a configured budget and alert, a runaway resource (e.g. an oversized VM left running, a misconfigured autoscale) can burn through a month's cloud budget before anyone notices.
Do: Set Cost Management budgets with action-group alerts at 50/80/100% thresholds per subscription.
Don't: Rely on manually checking the cost dashboard instead of configured budget alerts.
Example: az consumption budget create --budget-name monthly-budget --amount 5000 --time-grain Monthly

Topic: AKS pod identity vs managed identity
Keywords: aks, workload identity, managed identity, pod identity
Guidance: Baking service principal credentials into AKS pod environment variables or Secrets is a common leak vector; Azure Workload Identity federates pod ServiceAccounts to Entra ID without any stored secret.
Do: Use Azure AD Workload Identity (federated credentials) instead of storing service principal secrets in the cluster.
Don't: Store a service principal client secret as a Kubernetes Secret mounted into pods.

Topic: VM Scale Set health and upgrade policy
Keywords: vmss, scale set, rolling upgrade, health extension
Guidance: A VM Scale Set without the health extension and a rolling upgrade policy can push a bad image to every instance simultaneously with no automatic rollback.
Do: Enable the Application Health extension and configure a rolling upgrade policy with a max batch/unhealthy instance percentage.
Don't: Deploy VMSS updates with the default manual upgrade policy and no health probe.
Example: az vmss update --name myScaleSet --resource-group rg --set upgradePolicy.mode=Rolling

Keywords: azure sql, geo-redundant backup, failover group, point-in-time restore
Guidance: Locally-redundant backup storage means a regional outage takes both the database and its backups down together; geo-redundant storage and failover groups are needed for real DR.
Do: Configure geo-redundant backup storage and an auto-failover group for production Azure SQL/PostgreSQL.
Don't: Leave production database backup storage redundancy on the default locally-redundant setting.
Example: az sql db update --name mydb --resource-group rg --server myserver --backup-storage-redundancy Geo

Keywords: azure pipelines, yaml template, pipeline reuse, extends template
Guidance: Duplicating pipeline YAML across dozens of repos means a security or build-step fix has to be copy-pasted everywhere instead of updated once.
Do: Extract shared stages/jobs into YAML templates referenced via extends/template, versioned in a central repo.
Don't: Copy-paste an entire azure-pipelines.yml into every new repo.
